articleTitle: Brushless reluctance-motor drives
abstract: The variable-reluctance or switched-reluctance motor has some remarkable characteristics that make it attractive for dozens of applications. With CAD software now available, and many prototypes established, there should be few technicalbarriers between the laboratory and a number of successful niches in the drives market

articleTitle: System loss in a metropolitan utility network
abstract: System loss, namely the difference between electrical energy generated and actually sold, is very important, especially in the under-developed world. The article considers the various components of system loss and the economic considerations for system expansion, based on experience with the Calcutta metropolitan utility

articleTitle: Anticipating failures by dissolved-gas monitoring
abstract: Gas chromatography has for long been used to analyse gases dissolved in insulating oil which are generated as fault conditions develop, but it is an expensive laboratory-based technique. A rugged low-cost continuous monitoring device known as the Hydran system has been developed, and has been exhaustively tested in field use in North America

articleTitle: Transient switching overvoltages and compatibility of rotating machine insulation
abstract: The periodic upsurge of interest in the subject of switching overvoltages is usually based on a limited approach, often without numerate proof of the supposed practical criteria. This article shows that there is adequate background information to permit an informed view to be established, and demonstrates that the potential problem of a lack of understanding between the interrupter and rotating machine manufacturers is not real, although more information on interrupter performance is needed.

articleTitle: The 2000 MW HVDC link between England and France
abstract: The HVDC link across the English Channel has several innovative features. Techniques used in its construction together with recent developments have consolidated the viability of HVDC links for a variety of applications.

articleTitle: Voltage unbalance on rural systems
abstract: Unequal voltages or voltage unbalance on rural systems has been a known phenomenon for some time. This article discusses the causes and effects of voltage unbalance and gives a practical solution to the problem

articleTitle: Computer centre power engineering for the tropics
abstract: The climatic conditions in the tropics coupled with lack of infrastructure in the least-developed countries presents a ajor challenge to power engineers establishing and maintaining computer installations there

articleTitle: Influence of commutating reactance on the design of DC power supply converters
abstract: DC railway systems have now crystallised into the three major categories of 750V, 1500V and 3000V, the latter being applied to main-line systems and the first two mainly to urban masstransit or light-rail systems. This article reviews the significance of choice of transformer commutating reactance and highlights its importance in the design of DC substation convertors

articleTitle: Aluminium and energy
abstract: Aluminium smelters are very large consumers of both electricity and gas, and energy efficiency is absolutely vital. Today a modern smelter occupies a site outside Holyhead, and this factory is one of Europe's largest smelters. It consumes over 1800 million units of electricity a year which is supplied from a nuclear power plant

articleTitle: New options for 11 kV urban network design
abstract: The prospect of a major programme of switchgear replacement in the UK has led to a number of innovative proposals in the fields of plant, protection and network design. In addition to lowering the cost of systems, the new techniques enable the planned reliability of supply to be more closely matched to customers' requirements

articleTitle: The versatility of high-voltage fuses in the protection of distribution systems
abstract: Despite the challenges from other circuit-breaking devices, the high-voltage fuse is still a very important part of the protective scheme for HV distribution systems

articleTitle: The transformer feeder substation
abstract: In developing countries with high inner-city population density land prices for substation sites are extremely high. This article describes the merits of the transformer-feeder-substation concept as a low-cost, minimum-land-area solution for applications where simplicity, high service continuity and minimum maintenance are also primary considerations

articleTitle: The recruitment of power engineers, or the recruitment of power students?
Magnetic observations of earth-leakage currents from DC electric railways
abstract: Geomagnetic observatories have always complained about the interference from DC electric railways, but simple magnetic observations can give valuable information about the location and magnitude of earth-leakage currents

articleTitle: Electricity supply system on the London Underground
abstract: A deep-level tube railway with high traffic density has special requirements; also an interruption to any of the main or auxiliary services can be very serious. The present London Underground system, resulting from an amalgamation of separate undertakings, provides a tribute to the sound design and workmanship of the early equipment

articleTitle: Mechanical properties of copper in relation to power-transformer design
abstract: Pure soft copper in power-transformer windings may not be strong enough for units of low impedance or high rating. Increased strength may be obtained by alloying or cold working. Cold-worked copper will soften with time and temperature, so it is important to predict the effects of overloads and short circuits. A method of using Arrhenius plots to do this from laboratory measurements is described which shows that, for normal power transformers, conductor softening will not occur in normal service

articleTitle: Ohmic heating - a new process for the food industry
abstract: Public perception of what constitutes a healthy or high-quality product is leading manufacturers to exploit alternative processes and presentation. As a result, aseptically processed foods, which are cooked prior to packaging, are appearing in the shops. This article reviews the development of a novel electrical cooking process targeted for the modern aseptic process line

articleTitle: The electrical characteristics and selection of low-voltage power cables
abstract: This article analyses the electrical principles involved in lowvoltage (600/1000 V) power cables, many of which are applicable to power cables of higher voltages as well as wiring cables. Following a look at theoretical aspects, the article focuses on practical cable selection, mainly based on the author's experience in the Gulf countries of the Middle East

articleTitle: Early experience of an interconnected system in the Yemen Arab Republic
abstract: The provision of an interconnected power system for the Yemen Arab Republic provided the authors' company with major practical problems concerned with both the onerous conditions and also an unexpected geographical shift in demand growth

articleTitle: Wind gust phenomenon
Sri Lanka's Kotmale hydro project
abstract: The Kotmale hydropower project is a major component of the massive Mahaweli Ganga development. Adverse geological conditions at the originally planned dam site necessitated a change in the dam's location, and a comprehensive account of the investigations and project design is presented here, together with details of the main features of the scheme

articleTitle: Down to earth
Unique low-cost mini hydroelectric plant
abstract: A low-cost hydroelectric plant was designed to operate during the rainy season on the Perak River when the flow exceeded the capacity of the existing small hydroelectric station. Original ideas and simple methods can result in low capital costs

articleTitle: UPS comments
Improved efficiency in motor drives
abstract: With potential annual savings in view of over £30 million, Ewbank Preece has been commissioned by The Energy Technology Support Unit to manage a demonstration project to improve the cost effectiveness of electric-motor drives. Originally restricted to industry, the project hasbeen widened to include the commercial and domestic sectors, and also single-phase and fractional high-performance motor drives

articleTitle: Busbar comments
Three-phase coupling unit for partial discharge tests on cables
abstract: Polymeric insulation is increasingly being used for high-voltage cables. Partial discharge tests can be made with this coupling unit, which is suitable for testing such cables in the factory or in service

articleTitle: Instrumentation and monitoring equipment: provision for modern turbogenerators
abstract: The complexity of modern turbogenerator plant and instrumentation, and reduction in manning levels, means that instrumentation and monitoring equipment is usually located a central control room. It is now essential for instrumentation requirements to be specified at the same time as the main plant

articleTitle: Standby generators-is the electrical distribution system protected?
abstract: There is a continuously increasing number of electrical installations designed to operatefrom a normal 'mains' system that are called upon, from time to time, to operate from a standby or emergency generator. Due to the different natures of these two forms of electricity supplies it is by no means certain that the requirements for electrical safety can be complied with. The article investigates this problem and questions the present methods of specifying generators

articleTitle: Developments in fast reactors
abstract: Barnwood's Divisional Director explains some aspects of the work undertaken at Barnwood relating to the UK's fast reactor programme

articleTitle: Letter to the Editor
Overvoltage protection of gas-insulated substations
abstract: Increasing demand for electrical power in centres of large conurbations has led to the development of compact gasinsulated substations. For these it is not possible to follow established practice of fitting co-ordination gaps, and therefore surge arresters have to be used to limit overvoltages

articleTitle: The reason why
Power engineering lines
Welcome addition
Wind gust phenomena in the design of transmission lines
abstract: The question of the actual wind pressure that will, in practice, develop on the conductors is important in the design of overhead transmission lines. The fact that the maximum gust will not take effect over the full span of a line has a profound effect on line design

articleTitle: Powering ahead
Communications for distribution control rooms
abstract: Improved communications have allowed increased centralisation of power-system control. The days when customers phoning in complaints was a vital information source are disappearing

articleTitle: New generation of transmission system fault recorders: the CEGB experience
abstract: The CEGB is embarking on the installation of a new generation of transmission-system fault recorders which are microprocessor based. This article discusses the considerations which led to their installation, their in-service experience and future potential

articleTitle: What is power plant UK '87?
The Greater Dhaka Power Project
abstract: Since 1973, the power system of the Greater Dhaka area of Bangladesh has undergone major expansion. The demand for electricity in Dhaka is increasing rapidly and British engineers areworking on a project to update the system to enable it to cope with present and future demand.

articleTitle: Small motor drives expand their technology horizons
abstract: If we consider electrical technology to be divided into the two main areas of information processing and energy processing, the pervasiveness of drives technology will be immediately apparent. In developed economies about one-third of all primary energy is converted into electricity, and about twothirds of this electrical energy is subsequently converted in electric motors and drives

articleTitle: The control of large coal- and oil-fired generating units
abstract: In the continuing search for improved efficiency the CEGB is using sophisticated measuring equipment and computers to implement new control strategies. Frequent load changes rather than continuous steady operation have highlighted the need for improved plant control

articleTitle: Site test methods for high-voltage plant
abstract: The ability to assess the integrity of high-voltage insulation in installed electrical plant is important in determining future serviceability. Several techniques and purpose-built instruments which have been developed at CERL are usedto test a range of power-station and substation plant within the CEGB

articleTitle: System response studies incorporating real plant
abstract: A power-system simulator has been developed which can be attached to a real hydro-generator, making it possible to test the response of the hydro-generator with its associated governor, while apparently operating in any desired powersystem configuration

articleTitle: Technology transfer - a capenhurst perspective
abstract: This article is the first in a series devoted to the research being undertaken at Capenhurst, and the practical utilisation of that research in the industrial application of electricity

articleTitle: Electric sector planning: comparative experience in Asia and Pacific region
abstract: Power-suppy systems are highly complex and planning has developed into a sophisticated art. But it can no longer be undertaken in isolation, and a thorough understanding of the relationship between electricity and other economic and social parameters is essential. This article provides an insight into comparative experiences in electric sector planning in the Asia and Pacific region

articleTitle: Power lines, fields and good health
abstract: Recently some observers have questioned whether the electric and magnetic fields near power equipment are as innocuous as they appear to be. The author outlines studies and observations undertaken, and considers what precautions are appropriate

articleTitle: Electrical protection for domestic and small commercial installations
abstract: Because of the large number and widespread use of small electrical installations in the UK, protection of the user from potentially hazardous and dangerous situations is of vital importance. This article reviews present UK practice

articleTitle: Protection, control, alarm and auxiliary equipment for EHV substations
abstract: Faults on EHV systems can prove to be expensive for both supply authority and user. Careful selection of protective devices and ancillary equipment will minimise damage to plant and outage times

articleTitle: High-voltage polymeric insulated cables
abstract: The use of polymeric insulated cables in the UK as a rival to pressure-assisted cables has increased over recent years. Eastern Electricity was the first UK supply authority toundertake its own jointing work with the new material

articleTitle: Power-system planning under uncertainty - a new approach
abstract: Because of the long lead time between ordering equipment and commissioning, power-system planning has always catered explicitly for uncertainties. In the past, elaborate deterministic techniques have been used, but there are now doubts about whether the out-turn from such sophistication justifies the efforts required. Perhaps a more flexible, informal approach to both planning and uncertainty is the answer, e.g. to be able to alter course to take account of actual conditions; also, optimisation techniques might be changed. Unexpected power-system structures, reliability and loss levels, and also generation plant mixes, might well result, which are better for meeting actual requirements than those at present

articleTitle: The design of outdoor open-type EHV substations
abstract: What alternatives are available in the design of open-terminal EHV substations and what parameters affect the layout and hardware chosen?
